The present study aimed demonstrate the ability of APAP to change the brain and heart electrical activities, as early as significant increase in liver enzymes. Thus, a toxic dose of 1 g/kg was administered orally, and the animals were assessed every 3 h until 12 h for electroencephalography, electrocardiography and liver function data. The results showed that a toxic dose of APAP was capable of reducing brain electrical activity for the delta, theta, beta and gamma waves; however, the alpha wave activity was increased. In the heart, a reduced electrical activity was observed synchronously with the electroencephalogram. During the 12-h follow-up period, a significant increase in liver enzymes was observed. Taken together, we conclude that high doses of APAP can alter frequency brain oscillations and promote cardiac changes independently of liver damage in the first 12 h.

articles.title: Influence of drug loading and lipid dose on the in vivo performance of fenofibrate in medium- and long-chain triglyceride solutions.
articles.abstract: The influence of drug loading relative to the saturation solubility of a lipid vehicle and the administered lipid dose on the in vivo performance of lipid-based formulations remains incompletely understood. The present study investigated these formulation variables using fenofibrate dissolved in medium-chain triglyceride (MCT) and long-chain triglyceride (LCT) vehicles. The saturated solubility of fenofibrate in MCT and LCT at 37°C was assessed to determine suitable concentrations for in vivo studies. Fenofibrate showed higher solubility in MCT (185.8 mg/mL) compared to LCT (70.8 mg/mL), consistent with previous findings indicating lipid chain length affects solubilization. In vivo studies using rats involved administering a fixed lipid dose (2 mL/kg), with fenofibrate solubilized in the lipid solution at 25 %, 50 %, and 90 % of its saturation solubility. In a separate dose-escalation study, the relative drug loading was maintained at 90 % of its saturation solubility while the administered lipid volume, and consequently the fenofibrate dose, was increased. Pharmacokinetic analysis revealed that fenofibrate in MCT achieved higher plasma concentrations before dose correction, whereas fenofibrate in LCT led to higher plasma concentrations after dose correction. In the dose-escalation study, systemic exposure increased with increasing fenofibrate dose in both vehicles; however, less-than-dose-proportional increases in AUC0-30h and Cmax were observed over the dose ranges investigated. The deviation from proportionality in AUC0-30h was greater for MCT than for LCT, while decreasing dose-normalized exposure was observed for the higher doses of both vehicles. These findings demonstrate that drug loading relative to saturation solubility, lipid type, and administered lipid dose can all influence the in vivo performance of lipid-based formulations and should be considered when designing and comparing such formulations.

articles.title: Bufei Yishen formula ameliorates chronic obstructive pulmonary disease by restoring alveolar macrophage efferocytosis through Nrf2 activation.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Bufei Yishen formula (BYF) is a traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) prescription clinically used to improve pulmonary function and quality of life in patients with stable chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). However, its mechanism in regulating alveolar macrophage dysfunction remains unclear. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to determine whether BYF ameliorates COPD by restoring alveolar macrophage efferocytosis and to elucidate the involvement of nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (Nrf2) signaling. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) was used to characterize macrophage alterations in COPD. Cigarette smoke/Klebsiella pneumoniae-induced COPD animals and cigarette smoke extract (CSE) alveolar macrophages were employed to assess the effects of BYF on lung injury, inflammation, efferocytosis, oxidative stress, and Nrf2 signaling. Nrf2 involvement was verified with dimethyl fumarate and ML385, and Nrf2-binding constituents of BYF were identified using Affinity ultrafiltration-LC/MS (AU-LC/MS), molecular docking, and surface plasmon resonance (SPR). RESULTS: scRNA-seq analysis revealed that impaired macrophage efferocytosis is closely associated with COPD progression, identifying defective apoptotic cell clearance as a key pathological process. Consistently, in COPD animal models, BYF markedly improved pulmonary function, attenuated emphysematous and inflammatory lung lesions, reduced pro-inflammatory cytokine production, and corrected the imbalance between matrix metalloproteinases and their tissue inhibitor. To further clarify the underlying mechanism, RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) profiling of alveolar macrophages showed that BYF-regulated genes were mainly enriched in macrophage efferocytosis and Nrf2-related pathways. Mechanistically, both in vivo and in vitro experiments demonstrated that BYF activated Nrf2 signaling, promoted downstream HO-1 expression, reduced oxidative stress, and consequently restored cigarette smoke-impaired alveolar macrophage efferocytosis. Importantly, pharmacological inhibition of Nrf2 largely abolished the protective effects of BYF, whereas Nrf2 activation reproduced similar benefits, confirming the essential role of Nrf2 signaling in BYF-mediated macrophage protection. Furthermore, integrated AU-LC/MS, molecular docking, and SPR analyses identified nine constituents in BYF that interact with Nrf2, among which ononin exhibited the highest affinity (KD = 20.4 μM). Finally, ononin was verified to promote Nrf2 nuclear translocation, activate Nrf2 downstream genes, and may contribute to BYF-mediated efferocytosis restoration. CONCLUSION: BYF alleviates COPD-related lung injury, at least in part, by activating Nrf2 signaling and restoring alveolar macrophage efferocytosis. These findings provide mechanistic evidence supporting BYF as a potential therapeutic strategy for COPD.

articles.title: Dendrobium huoshanense ameliorates spermatogenesis disorder in rats through modulating m6A methylation modification and the NRF2-GPX4/TLR4-MyD88 signaling pathways.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Spermatogenesis disorder (SPD) has become a significant factor affecting male reproductive health. Dendrobium huoshanense (DH) is a rare and precious perennial orchid used in traditional Chinese medicine to nourish yin and tonify the kidney, but its mechanism in improving spermatogenic function remains unclear. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aims to elucidate the pharmacodynamic material basis and mechanism of action of DH in improving SPD. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Male rats were divided into blank control, model, positive drug, and DH high, medium, and low dose groups. SPD model was induced by Tripterygium wilfordii glycosides (TWG). Testicular histopathology, fibrosis, apoptosis, and protein levels of METTL3, METTL14, METTL16, WTAP, ALKBH5, TLR4, NRF2, and GPX4 were assessed. m6A-seq, metabolomics, and transcriptomics were performed to analyze m6A modifications and methyl donor abundance. Active components were identified via high-resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS). RESULTS: DH aqueous extract attenuated spermatogenic cell loss, seminiferous tubules basement membrane fibrosis and germ cell apoptosis in SPD model group, up-regulated the protein expression levels of METTL3, METTL14, METTL16, WTAP, ALKBH5, NRF2, and GPX4 in testicular tissues of the model group, promoted consumption of carnitine derivative methyl donors, and increased m6A modification of Sox family (Sox4, Sox9, Sox11, Sox13, etc.), Nrf2, and Gpx4 in germ cells. The active components identified in DH aqueous extract primarily included bibenzyl and flavonoid compounds. CONCLUSION: DH up-regulates the METTL3/METTL14 complex, promoting methyl donor consumption and enhancing m6A modification and protein expression of Sox9, Gpx4, and Nrf2, thereby alleviating oxidative stress and restoring impaired spermatogenesis.

articles.title: Stigmasterol suppresses macrophage-mediated inflammatory amplification in acute pancreatitis through PPAR-γ-dependent macrophage reprogramming.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Glycine max (L.) Merr. (G. max; soybean), a widely cultivated medicinal and edible plant, has been traditionally used in Chinese medicine and dietary practices for maintaining digestive health. Stigmasterol (STG), a naturally occurring dietary phytosterol widely distributed in G. max and other edible and medicinal plants, is investigated here as a bioactive dietary constituent rather than as an isolate from a documented traditional remedy specifically used for acute pancreatitis (AP). STG has attracted increasing attention due to its anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory activities; however, its potential role and underlying mechanisms in AP remain unclear. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to investigate the protective effects of STG against AP and elucidate its role in regulating macrophage-mediated inflammatory amplification. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Publicly available transcriptomic, spatial transcriptomic, and single-cell RNA sequencing datasets were downloaded and bioinformatically analyzed to identify key inflammatory pathways and cellular interactions in AP. The protective effects of STG were evaluated in AP mice and compared with ulinastatin (UTI). Network pharmacology, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and cellular thermal shift assays (CETSA) were applied to identify STG targets. RAW264.7 macrophages and AR42J pancreatic acinar cells were used for in vitro validation, including peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma (PPAR-γ) knockdown and co-culture experiments. RESULTS: Multi-omics analyses revealed that Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4)-mediated nuclear factor kappa-light-chain-enhancer of activated B cells (NF-κB) signaling is a central inflammatory pathway in AP and is closely associated with macrophage-related high mobility group box 1 (HMGB1) signaling. STG treatment alleviated pancreatic injury, inhibited NF-κB activation, and regulated macrophage polarization with comparable efficacy to UTI. Integrated pharmacological analyses and CETSA supported PPAR-γ as a key functional mediator and candidate molecular target of STG. STG regulated macrophage polarization and reduced extracellular HMGB1 release from activated macrophages in a PPAR-γ-dependent manner, accompanied by attenuation of macrophage-mediated TLR4/NF-κB-associated inflammatory responses in pancreatic acinar cells. CONCLUSIONS: Although further validation in additional experimental models is warranted, STG ameliorates AP through PPAR-γ-dependent remodeling of macrophage immune responses, accompanied by reduced extracellular HMGB1 release and attenuation of TLR4/NF-κB-associated inflammatory signaling.

articles.title: Celastrol Targets FGFR1 to Attenuate Synovial Inflammation and Joint Destruction in Rheumatoid Arthritis.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Natural products from traditional medicinal plants are valuable sources for discovering bioactive molecules targeting disease-relevant pathways. Tripterygium wilfordii Hook. f. has been traditionally used in Chinese medicine for rheumatic and inflammatory disorders. In this study, celastrol, a pentacyclic triterpenoid originally isolated from T. wilfordii, was identified through target-oriented natural product screening as a candidate FGFR1-binding compound. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to define the pathogenic role of fibroblast growth factor receptor 1 (FGFR1) in rheumatoid arthritis progression and to determine whether celastrol, identified by target-oriented natural product screening, attenuates synovial inflammation and joint destruction through FGFR1 signaling suppression. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Multi-omics analyses, AAV-mediated FGFR1 gain- and loss-of-function experiments in collagen-induced arthritis rats, and MH7A fibroblast-like synoviocyte (FLS) assays were used to investigate FGFR1 function. SCENIC and CUT&Tag analyses were performed to examine FGFR1-associated transcriptional regulation. High-throughput virtual screening of a natural product library, surface plasmon resonance, and LC-MS/MS were used to identify and validate celastrol as an FGFR1-binding compound, followed by in vitro and in vivo assessment of its effects on FGFR1-driven pathology. RESULTS: FGFR1 overexpression was associated with increased synovial inflammation, cartilage damage, and bone erosion in collagen-induced arthritis rats, whereas FGFR1 knockdown showed protective effects. Mechanistically, FGFR1 appeared to enhance STAT1-mediated TGFB1 transcription, thereby promoting extracellular matrix remodeling, collagen deposition, and FLS invasion. High-throughput virtual screening of 4,667 natural compounds, followed by surface plasmon resonance and LC-MS/MS validation, identified celastrol as a candidate FGFR1-binding compound. Celastrol attenuated FGFR1-STAT1-TGF-β1 signaling and reduced extracellular matrix-related protein expression, FLS invasion, synovial fibrosis, and joint destruction. CONCLUSIONS: Celastrol attenuates rheumatoid arthritis progression, at least in part, by targeting FGFR1 and suppressing the FGFR1-STAT1-TGF-β1 axis; these mechanistic findings, primarily derived from the MH7A cell line, warrant further validation in primary RA-FLS.

articles.title: Natural (+)-Camphor Alleviates Migraine Induced by Reserpine with Local Cerebral Vasospasm via Inhibiting p38β MAPK/ATF2 Pathway.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: The pathogenesis of migraine model by reserpine with local cerebral vasospasm matches the characteristics of migraine with cold-coagulation in traditional Chinese medicine (TCM). Natural (+)-camphor (NC) is one of the Chinese herbal medicines with heat property, which is known to be effective in expelling cold and alleviating pain in TCM. AIM OF THE STUDY: The proteomic analysis of migraine model by reserpine with local cerebral vasospasm and effect of NC was investigated to delineate the possible underlying mechanism. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Mice brain proteomic analysis was carried out by data-independent acquisition mass spectrometry. The biological information of differentially-expressed proteins was analyzed based on Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes analysis. Animal behavior, brain histopathology and NO generation assay were observed. RESULTS: Compared with normal, migraine mice had lower pain threshold, severe brain lesion and reduced NO content in serum. NC could improve pathological change. A total of 479 differentially-expressed proteins were identified. 8significant differential proteins were focused based on analysis. The distinctive proteins are commonly related to MAPK signaling pathway, and p38β MAPK was validated, which was excessively expressed in migraine mice. NC could mitigate cold-coagulation migraine symptoms by regulating NO production via inhibiting p38β MAPK/ATF2 pathway. CONCLUSION: NC showed analgesic effect, and p38β MAPK was most likely to be the targets against vasospastic cold-coagulation migraine.

articles.title: Identification of Stroke as the Predominant Hypoxia-Associated Cerebrovascular Disease: Integrated NHANES Evidence and Mechanistic Insights into JUN-Mediated Endothelial Injury and Protection by Licarin B.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Hypoxia, a featured condition of high-altitude regions, contributes to the development of a wide range of cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases. However, the cardiovascular or cerebrovascular disease most strongly associated with hypoxia, along with its underlying molecular mechanisms and potential therapeutic targets, remains incompletely understood. Sanwei Tanxiang Powder (SWTX) is a classical Tibetan prescription that has long been used to improve blood circulation and alleviate hypoxia-related cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disorders. Licarin B is a bioactive constituent of SWTX with potential therapeutic value. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to identify the cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disease most strongly associated with hypoxia, investigate its underlying molecular mechanisms, and explore the protective effects and molecular targets of licarin B against hypoxia-associated cerebrovascular injury. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We employed an integrative strategy combining population-based epidemiological analysis, transcriptomics, network pharmacology, single-cell RNA sequencing, and experimental validation to systematically investigate hypoxia-associated cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases and their pathogenic mechanisms. Human cerebral microvascular endothelial cells (hCMEC/D3), were used to evaluate the effects of hypoxia and licarin B on oxidative stress, inflammatory responses, nitric oxide production, and endothelial function. The therapeutic efficacy of licarin B was further evaluated in a mouse model of acute ischemic stroke induced by middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO). RESULTS: Epidemiological analysis identified ischemic stroke as the cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disease most strongly associated with hypoxia, as indicated by low hemoglobin levels. Multi-omics analyses revealed that hypoxia-associated stroke-related genes were predominantly enriched in inflammatory and oxidative stress pathways, with JUN identified as a key hypoxia-related stroke gene (HRSG). Single-cell transcriptomic analysis of murine brain tissue further demonstrated that JUN was relatively highly expressed in endothelial cells and positively associated with pro-inflammatory immune cell infiltration. In hCMEC/D3 cells exposed to hypoxia, JNK phosphorylation and JUN expression levels were markedly increased, accompanied by reactive oxygen species accumulation, impaired nitric oxide production, and enhanced expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines. Network pharmacology and molecular docking identified licarin B, a bioactive constituent of SWTX, as a candidate compound predicted to target JUN. In hypoxia-exposed hCMEC/D3 cells, licarin B significantly suppressed JUN expression, mitigated hypoxia-induced oxidative stress and inflammatory responses, and preserved endothelial barrier integrity, whereas JUN overexpression or JNK activation partially abrogated these protective effects. Furthermore, in a middle cerebral artery occlusion mouse model, licarin B administration reduced cerebral infarct volume, alleviated ischemic brain injury, suppressed the JNK/JUN signaling axis and pro-inflammatory cytokine expression, and improved neurological function. CONCLUSIONS: This study identifies the hypoxia-JNK/JUN axis as a critical mediator of microvascular endothelial dysfunction during ischemic stroke and highlights licarin B, a bioactive constituent of SWTX, as a promising therapeutic candidate for hypoxia-associated cerebrovascular injury.

articles.title: Exemestane induces a reduction in hematopoietic stem cells and immunotoxicity in zebrafish larvae by downregulating Wnt signaling pathway.
articles.abstract: Exemestane is a third-generation aromatase inhibitor commonly prescribed for estrogen-dependent breast cancer. Given the widespread clinical use of exemestane, various adverse reactions have been reported. However, there are only a limited number of reports on the effects on the immune system. Therefore, it is essential to examine its potential toxicity and mechanism of action. In this research, zebrafish were employed as a model organism to examine the impact of exemestane on embryonic development and immune function. The larvae that were fertilized 8 hours post-fertilization (hpf) were respectively exposed to exemestane solutions of different concentrations (0.9, 1.8 and 2.7 mg/L).The results demonstrated that exemestane exposure induced a concentration-dependent reduction in larval body length and an increase in yolk sac area, indicative of developmental toxicity. Subsequently, exemestane was administered to the corresponding transgenic fish lines, and it was observed that the numbers of hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs), neutrophils, macrophages, and thymic T cells exhibited dose dependent decreases during exposure. Concurrently, exemestane-exposed zebrafish exhibited significantly elevated oxidative stress levels and an increased incidence of apoptotic cells. Gene expression analysis demonstrated that the immune-related gene NF-kB was downregulated, whereas tlr2 and tlr3 were upregulated in response to treatment. Notably, no significant alterations were observed in the expression levels of il-1b, prl, or lakros. . The use of astaxanthin (AS) and the wnt signaling pathway activator BML-284 can alleviate the embryonic immunotoxicity caused by exemestane. In conclusion, our study represents the first comprehensive evaluation of the immunomodulatory effects of exemestane on zebrafish larvae. These effects are likely associated with exemestane-induced elevation of oxidative stress and suppression of the Wnt signaling pathway.

articles.title: The Coherence Response Index: predicted microRNA targets show no coherent regulation in chemically exposed mouse embryonic stem cells.
articles.abstract: Toxicogenomic studies increasingly promote microRNA (miRNA) expression changes as chemical-toxicity biomarkers and infer their meaning from computationally predicted messenger RNA (mRNA) targets, rarely testing those predictions against matched mRNA data. We present the Coherence Response Index (CRI), an open, expression-matched check of whether a responsive miRNA's predicted targets shift in the expected direction. CRI recovered target repression in two positive controls: miRNA-mimic transfection (6/6 productive; AUC≈0.73) and, at endogenous stoichiometry in mouse embryonic stem cells (mESCs), Dicer1 knockout (137 of 412 evaluable expressed miRNAs productive, against 35 of 211 non-expressed controls); spiked-in coherent shifts of 0.1 log2 units were detected in 77% of tests. We then applied CRI to two of our own published datasets from the same RNA preparations of mESCs exposed for 24 h to nine chemicals (paired small- and long-RNA-seq, duplicate). Across 225 miRNA×chemical tests, predicted targets showed no coherent regulation (AUC mean 0.489, SD 0.050); a single borderline call (miR-200a-5p, DEHP) was not robust to resampling. Restricting the background to protein-coding genes added significant shifts, but not in the miRNA's direction (8 coherent, 12 anti-coherent). Separately, the published fold changes of the mapped benzene biomarkers do not reproduce (sign agreement 54%, Spearman ρ = 0.11): they arise from isoform-level quantification and a zero-replacement log-ratio estimator that, on identical data, yields thousands of extreme values that vanish under a pseudocount estimator. In this short-exposure mESC screening design, predicted-target enrichment did not describe observed regulation; CRI offers a reusable check wherever a matched mRNA layer exists.

articles.title: Acaudiolide attenuates MASH-related liver fibrosis through covalent engagement of SMAD4 and blockade of p-SMAD2/3 nuclear translocation.
articles.abstract: Hepatic stellate cell (HSC) activation is a central driver of fibrosis progression in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), yet effective antifibrotic pharmacotherapies remain limited. Here, we identify acaudiolide, a sulfur-bridged symmetric dimeric macrodiolide isolated from the fungus Acaulium sp. H-JQSF, as a natural-product lead that suppresses HSC activation and experimental liver fibrosis. In a Western diet (WD)/CCl4 murine model of MASH, acaudiolide reduced collagen deposition, alpha-smooth muscle actin (α-SMA) expression and fibrogenic gene expression. Transcriptomic profiling of HSCs showed that acaudiolide antagonized transforming growth factor-β1 (TGF-β1)-driven profibrotic programs. Mechanistically, acaudiolide did not measurably alter SMAD2/3 phosphorylation but markedly reduced the nuclear accumulation of phosphorylated SMAD2/3 (p-SMAD2/3). Integration of Connectivity Map (CMap) analysis with isotopic tandem orthogonal proteolysis-activity-based protein profiling (isoTOP-ABPP) chemical proteomics nominated SMAD4 as a candidate covalent target of acaudiolide. Covalent docking suggested Cys363 as a potential engagement site, and co-immunoprecipitation showed that acaudiolide weakened the association of SMAD4 with p-SMAD2/3. These findings support a model in which acaudiolide interferes with SMAD complex assembly, thereby attenuating TGF-β-dependent profibrotic transcription and HSC activation. Collectively, our data nominate acaudiolide as a preclinical antifibrotic lead and SMAD4 as a potentially tractable downstream node for pharmacological modulation of TGF-β signaling in MASH-related fibrosis.

articles.title: Tirzepatide alleviates hepatic steatosis and inflammation in MASLD partly through suppression of macrophage Dectin-1/Syk/NF-κB signaling.
articles.abstract: Metabolic stress, hepatic lipid accumulation, and macrophage-associated sterile inflammation are closely involved in the development of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). Tirzepatide improves metabolic outcomes, but its effects on macrophage inflammatory signaling in MASLD remain unclear. This study investigated the protective effects of tirzepatide against high-fat, high-fructose diet (HFHFD)-induced MASLD and examined the potential involvement of macrophage Dectin-1/spleen tyrosine kinase (Syk)/nuclear factor-κB (NF-κB) signaling. After 7 weeks of HFHFD feeding to establish the MASLD model, male C57BL/6J mice received tirzepatide (10 nmol/kg, subcutaneously, every 3 days) for an additional 7 weeks. Biochemical assays, histology, hepatic RNA sequencing (RNA-seq), RT-qPCR, Western blotting, and immunofluorescence were performed. Palmitic acid (PA)-stimulated RAW264.7 cells, siRNA-mediated Dectin-1 knockdown, and a RAW264.7 cell-derived conditioned medium-based macrophage-hepatocyte indirect interaction model were used for mechanistic validation. Tirzepatide treatment improved HFHFD-induced metabolic dysfunction, liver injury, hepatic steatosis, and inflammatory responses in mice. RNA-seq revealed enrichment of C-type lectin receptor and NF-κB signaling pathways, while HFHFD-induced Clec7a upregulation was reversed by tirzepatide. Tirzepatide reduced hepatic macrophage accumulation, Dectin-1 expression, and Syk/p65 phosphorylation. In PA-stimulated RAW264.7 cells, tirzepatide suppressed pro-inflammatory cytokine expression and secretion and inhibited Dectin-1/Syk/NF-κB activation. Conditioned medium from tirzepatide-treated RAW264.7 cells attenuated lipid accumulation and abnormalities in lipid metabolism- and inflammation-related gene expression in HepG2 cells. Dectin-1 knockdown itself attenuated PA-induced inflammatory responses and was associated with a reduced additional response to tirzepatide. These findings suggest that tirzepatide alleviates HFHFD-induced MASLD, with suppression of macrophage Dectin-1/Syk/NF-κB signaling potentially contributing to these effects.

articles.title: Evaluation of EVT401, a P2X7 Receptor Antagonist, in Healthy Chinese Participants: a first-in-human, double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, dose-escalation trial.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: As a critical hub between extracellular danger signals and intracellular inflammation, the P2X7 receptor centrally drives synovitis and joint destruction in rheumatoid arthritis, making it an attractive therapeutic target. This study reported the first-in-human data for EVT401, an orally administered P2X7 receptor antagonist. METHODS: A phase I trial was conducted in healthy Chinese participants aged 18 to 50 years, encompassing a single ascending dose study (40-1920 mg), a food-effect study (960 mg), and a multiple ascending dose study (480 mg-960 mg). This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial evaluated safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetic characteristics as primary outcomes. Exploratory outcomes assessed the pharmacodynamic effects of EVT401 on cytokines and immune cells. RESULTS: A total of 101 participants were enrolled in the trial. Only a few mild, transient adverse events were reported during the trial, and no serious adverse events were observed. The pharmacokinetic data obtained from each study were consistent, with Tmax ranging from 0.5 to 2.75 hours and mean half-lives from 12.7 to 28.3 hours. Dose-exposure analysis demonstrated that EVT401 had nonlinear pharmacokinetic characteristics. The food effect study showed that a high-fat meal increased the absorption and systemic exposure of EVT401. Exploratory pharmacodynamic results suggested that EVT401 exhibited an anti-inflammatory trend by upregulating regulatory T cells and suppressing helper T cells. CONCLUSIONS: The first-in-human data for EVT401 have demonstrated a favorable safety profile and encouraging pharmacodynamic properties, providing strong support for its further clinical development. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: This trial has been registered with the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2600126139, ChiCTR2600125998).

articles.title: Phosphatase and tensin homolog (PTEN) drives perivascular adipose tissue (PVAT) dysfunction in rats fed a high-sugar diet.
articles.abstract: AIMS: Perivascular adipose tissue (PVAT) dysfunction is a hallmark of obesity-associated vascular disease; however, the molecular mechanisms involved remain incompletely understood. We investigated whether phosphatase and tensin homolog (PTEN) contributes to PVAT dysfunction in male and female rats fed a high-sugar (HS) diet. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A total of 24 Wistar rats (12 males and 12 females) were fed a control (CT) or HS diet for 14 weeks. Vascular reactivity was assessed in aortic rings with or without PVAT. PTEN expression, Akt and eNOS phosphorylation, and nitric oxide (NO) bioavailability were evaluated in PVAT. The functional role of PTEN-Akt signaling was investigated using a PTEN inhibitor and an Akt activator. KEY FINDINGS: The HS diet induced obesity in both sexes. However, PVAT dysfunction occurred exclusively in males, as evidenced by loss of the anticontractile effect of PVAT and impaired endothelium-dependent relaxation. These alterations were accompanied by decreased NO bioavailability, increased PTEN expression, and reduced levels of phosphorylated Akt and eNOS in PVAT. In contrast, female rats maintained normal PVAT function and NO signaling despite developing obesity. Pharmacological inhibition of PTEN or activation of Akt restored the anticontractile properties of PVAT and improved endothelial relaxation in HS-fed males. Furthermore, PTEN inhibition normalized NO production in PVAT. SIGNIFICANCE: PTEN is a mediator of obesity-induced PVAT dysfunction in male rats through suppression of the Akt/eNOS/NO signaling pathway. These findings identify PTEN as potential therapeutic target for obesity-associated vascular dysfunction and highlight important sex-dependent differences in PVAT biology.

articles.title: Alphitolic acid suppressed osteoclast differentiation via hindering Cox-2/NF-κB signal pathway and alleviated titanium particle-induced bone loss in vivo.
articles.abstract: Total joint arthroplasty (TJA) effectively improves the quality of life for patients with end-stage joint disorders. However, aseptic loosening caused by titanium (Ti) wear debris-induced osteolysis remains the leading cause of implant failure and revision surgeries. In this study, we investigated the therapeutic potential of alphitolic acid (ALA), a pentacyclic triterpenoid with known anti-inflammatory properties, against Ti particle-induced osteolysis and explored its underlying mechanisms. Network pharmacology analysis combined with molecular docking predicted that ALA targets key regulators of osteoclastogenesis, including PTGS2, with favorable binding affinity. In vitro, non-cytotoxic concentrations of ALA dose-dependently suppressed RANKL-induced osteoclast differentiation in BMMs, as evidenced by reduced TRAP-positive multinucleated cells and downregulation of osteoclast-specific genes. ALA also impaired F-actin ring formation and bone resorption activity. Mechanistically, ALA selectively inhibited phosphorylation of NF-κB p65 without affecting MAPK or AKT signaling pathways, leading to diminished expression and nuclear translocation of NFATc1 and c-Fos. RNA-sequencing further revealed that ALA downregulated Ptgs2 (COX-2) and its downstream targets, suggesting disruption of a COX-2/NF-κB feedback loop. In a murine calvarial osteolysis model, daily subcutaneous administration of ALA (15 mg/kg) significantly attenuated Ti particle-induced bone destruction, improving bone volume by 58% and reducing osteoclast numbers by 68% compared to vehicle-treated controls, as confirmed by micro-computed tomography and histomorphometric analysis. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that ALA effectively inhibits Ti particle-induced osteolysis by suppressing osteoclastogenesis through blockade of the NF-κB signaling pathway and modulation of PTGS2, positioning ALA as a promising natural compound for the prevention of periprosthetic osteolysis in TJA.

articles.title: Predicting drug-drug interaction and optimal dosing regimens of rivaroxaban combined with ceritinib using physiologically based pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic modeling.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Direct oral anticoagulants like rivaroxaban are globally recommended for cancer-associated thrombosis. However, co-administration with the targeted ALK inhibitor ceritinib in lung cancer patients poses a critical risk of drug-drug interactions (DDI) due to potent CYP3A4 inhibition, lacking quantitative clinical assessments. OBJECTIVES: To develop and validate physiologically based pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic (PBPK/PD) models to quantitatively assess this specific DDI and provide model-predicted dosing strategies. METHODS: A hybrid "bottom-up" and "top-down" modeling strategy was employed within PK-Sim®. The rivaroxaban model integrated complex hepatic metabolic pathways (CYP3A4, CYP2J2, non-CYP hydrolysis) and active transport (P-gp, BCRP). The ceritinib model incorporated competitive and time-dependent CYP3A4 inhibition parameters. DDI simulations were conducted in a virtual Chinese population. The established model was applied to an exploratory clinical case, comparing its predictions against steady-state plasma concentrations determined via highly specific UPLC-MS/MS from a real-world ALK-positive non-small-cell lung cancer patient. RESULTS: Simulations demonstrated that concomitant administration of ceritinib (450 mg qd) increased rivaroxaban AUC by 52%-63% and Cmax by 49%-59%. Consequently, the exploratory risk of major bleeding elevated to 1.64- to 1.79-fold that of rivaroxaban monotherapy, aligning closely with observed clinical case data. However, reducing rivaroxaban from 20 mg qd to 12.5 mg qd (normal or mildly impaired renal function), and from 15 mg qd to 10 mg qd (moderate renal impairment), yielded exposure and bleeding risk comparable to standard monotherapy. CONCLUSIONS: Our model predicts that ceritinib co-administration substantially elevates rivaroxaban exposure and exploratory major bleeding risk. Dose adjustment, alternative therapies, or close clinical monitoring are recommended to ensure patient safety.

articles.title: Molecular dynamics and clustering analysis of self-assembled biodegradable polymeric nanoparticles for insulin encapsulation.
articles.abstract: Self-assembled biodegradable polymeric nanoparticles are promising carriers for protein therapeutics such as insulin, whose clinical administration remains challenging. Accordingly, we used molecular dynamics (MD) simulations to investigate how poly (lactic acid) (PLA), poly (ethylene glycol)-PLA (PEG-PLA), poly (lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA), PEG-PLGA, and methoxy-PEG (mPEG)-PLGA oligomers self-assemble on the insulin surface. We further applied essential dynamics and K-means clustering analyses to evaluate protein motions and characterize oligomer assembly states, respectively. We observed no meaningful loss of insulin structural stability in the oligomer-containing systems, and most formed compact, approximately spherical aggregates. In contrast, mPEG-PLGA showed limited protein coverage because its oligomer chains predominantly assembled rather than contacting insulin. PEG incorporation into PLA and PLGA increased oligomer-insulin interactions, primarily governed by van der Waals (vdW) and hydrophobic contributions. Essential dynamics analysis showed no marked changes in insulin's dominant motion patterns, while PEG-PLA, PLGA, and PEG-PLGA sampled comparatively compact conformational states. Clustering analysis categorized the sampled configurations into three structurally distinct assembly states, with compact configurations occurring more frequently in these three systems. Integrating triplicate trajectories, residue-level contact and relative energetic analyses, essential dynamics, and replicate-aware clustering provides a comparative atomistic description of how oligomer chemistry and architecture influence insulin stability and motions, oligomer-insulin adsorption, and early self-assembly behavior. These findings may support computational screening and subsequent experimental evaluation of polymeric carriers for insulin and other protein therapeutics.

articles.title: Dietary iron supplementation attenuates doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity by improving myocardial iron homeostasis and reducing ferroptosis-associated injury in mice.
articles.abstract: Iron deficiency frequently accompanies chronic heart failure (CHF) and is linked to adverse clinical outcomes. Although intravenous iron replacement has shown clinical benefit in heart failure, whether increasing dietary iron intake can provide cardioprotective effects remains uncertain. In this study, we examined the effects of dietary iron supplementation in a murine model of doxorubicin (Dox)-induced cardiotoxicity. Mice were treated with Dox at 2.5 mg/kg by intraperitoneal injection once weekly for 6 weeks and received either standard chow containing 45 ppm iron or ferric citrate-enriched chow containing 5,000 ppm iron. We assessed cardiac function, myocardial injury, fibrosis, apoptosis, mitochondrial ultrastructure, oxidative stress, transcriptomic changes, and iron metabolism-related proteins through echocardiography, histological examination, biochemical assays, RNA sequencing, and Western blot analysis. In Dox-treated mice, the iron-enriched diet was associated with better survival and cardiac performance, together with less myocardial damage, fibrosis, apoptosis, mitochondrial injury, and oxidative stress. Transcriptomic analysis revealed enrichment of ferroptosis-related pathways in hearts exposed to Dox. Dox exposure also disturbed cardiac iron handling, as reflected by abnormal myocardial iron distribution, higher transferrin receptor 1 (TFR1) and nuclear receptor coactivator 4 (NCOA4) abundance, and lower ferritin heavy chain 1 (FTH1) expression. Most of these changes shifted toward control levels after dietary iron supplementation, while SLC7A11 abundance was unaffected. Taken together, our findings suggest that dietary iron supplementation mitigates Dox-induced cardiac injury, accompanied by improved myocardial iron homeostasis and attenuation of ferroptosis-related injury. Changes in NCOA4 and FTH1 abundance may reflect altered ferritin turnover and potentially contribute to the observed cardioprotective effects.

articles.title: A poly(vinyl alcohol)-based dissolvable bilayer film for buccal and sublingual delivery of FITC-dextran 4000 as a model macromolecule.
articles.abstract: Oromucosal administration of peptides remains challenging due to the limited permeability of the buccal and sublingual mucosa to hydrophilic macromolecules. This study evaluated the permeation-enhancing performance of the bile salt, sodium glycodeoxycholate (GDC), by investigating its incorporation into a semi-dissolvable bilayer film platform using fluorescein isothiocyanate-labelled dextran 4000 (FD4) as a model macromolecule. In human TR-146 buccal epithelial monolayers, GDC increased FD4 permeability in a concentration-dependent manner, with 1 mM identified as the highest non-cytotoxic concentration. In ex vivo porcine buccal mucosae, 20 mM GDC enhanced FD4 permeation to 6.9% after 3 h (Papp = 6.1 × 10-6 cm/s) while histology was maintained. Ventral lingual mucosae consistently exhibited greater permeability than buccal mucosae, with 20 mM GDC increasing FD4 permeation to 11.4% after 3 h (Papp = 12.6 × 10-6 cm/s). A poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA)/sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (Na-CMC)-based mucoadhesive layer with an ethyl cellulose backing was selected as the prototype bilayer film based on physicochemical properties and in vitro release characteristics. Incorporation of an equivalent GDC amount into bilayer films entrapping FD4 resulted in permeation of 0.7% and 3.5% across buccal and ventral lingual mucosae after 3 h, respectively. Histological and confocal fluorescence analyses confirmed enhanced tissue penetration and modulation of epithelial barrier structures following GDC exposure. While GDC presented in solution produced higher FD4 permeation than from films, the latter is a dosage form that can be translated to patients. These findings show that mucosal site is an important consideration in the development of GDC-loaded bilayer films and support further evaluation of the ventral lingual/sublingual region for peptide and other macromolecule delivery.

articles.title: Dose recovery after repeated drug administration via nasogastric feeding tubes under clinically relevant conditions: a novel in vitro model.
articles.abstract: Administration of solid oral drug products via enteral feeding tubes (EFTs) is common due to the lack of suitable alternatives but is associated with substantial risk of drug loss. A novel in vitro setup was developed to simulate clinical administration, considering patient supine positioning, tube temperature control, tube diameter and material, and nutritional formula supply. Drug recovery of furosemide and levothyroxine was evaluated under best- and worst-case administration conditions over several days. Under best case conditions, including multiple syringe and tube flushing steps, recovery exceeded 90 percent for both drugs. Under worst-case conditions, where flushing was omitted, furosemide recovery on day one reached approximately 90 percent in 14 French tubes and 70 percent in 10 French tubes, while levothyroxine recovery was around 80 percent across all tubes. Drug recovery in 14 French tubes declined over time, reflecting sedimentation, incomplete syringe emptying, and interactions with nutritional formula. During nutritional supply, agglutination of nutrient formula and increased back pressure occurred, and residual deposits and bacterial colonization were observed at the tube interior. These findings underscore the critical role of flushing syringes and EFTs to maximize dose recovery and prevent tube obstruction. The study demonstrates that clinically relevant administration factors including tube diameter, duration of nutrition, and procedural adherence substantially influence delivered drug doses. The presented in vitro model provides a standardized, practice-oriented platform for evaluating drug recovery through EFTs, supporting optimization of clinical administration protocols and guiding future recommendations.

articles.title: Molecular pathways implicated in antidepressant actions exhibits diurnal fluctuations in the prefrontal cortex and hippocampus of adult male and female mice.
articles.abstract: Epidemiological and experimental studies have demonstrated a bidirectional relationship between mood disorders and the circadian system, with disrupted circadian rhythms contributing to depressive states, and their restoration playing a key role in antidepressants effects. In this context, we sought to examine whether selected molecular pathways implicated in antidepressant responses exhibit diurnal regulatory patterns. Naïve adult male and female C57BL/6 mice were euthanized at 3-hour intervals beginning at Zeitgeber Time 0 (ZT0), and hippocampal (HC) and medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) tissues were collected for RT-qPCR and western blot analyses. We observed statistically significant diurnal rhythmicity in all analyzed transcripts (cFos, Arc, Nr4a1, Dusp1, Dusp5, and Dusp6) in both HC and mPFC samples, with peak expression occurring during the dark (active) phase (ZT15-18). Phosphorylation levels of TrkBY816 (tropomyosin-related kinase) and GSK3βS9 (glycogen synthase kinase 3β) also showed patterns suggestive of temporal rhythmicity, peaking during the light (inactive) phase. Levels of p-ERK2T185/Y187 (extracellular-signal regulated kinase) did not display rhythmic fluctuations, but peaked during the light phase in the HC, especially in males. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that antidepressant-related signaling is subject to diurnal regulation, highlighting the importance of integrating circadian biology and time-of-day as relevant variables in the development of translationally relevant antidepressant research.

articles.title: Evaluation of the spectral information acquired by an in-line high-speed near-infrared reflection sensor in a tableting environment.
articles.abstract: Near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy is widely used in process analytical technology during manufacturing of tablets. Therefore, the aim of the present study was to investigate an NIR sensor capable of in-line monitoring of tablets during manufacturing regarding the influence of the tablet temperature on the spectral data and the relevance of the effective penetration depth of the NIR radiation. The influence of the temperature was assessed by subjecting two tablet formulations to a temperature program while simultaneously recording NIR spectra. Whereas chemometric methods, such as differentiation techniques and variable selection merely suppressed the temperature influence, a novel correction method based on the linearity between temperature and NIR spectra showed promising results in reducing this influence, while maintaining the relevant spectral features. To determine the effective NIR penetration depth of the tablets, bilayer tablets with a bottom layer consisting of polytetrafluoroethylene and a top layer with variable thickness consisting of a common immediate-release tablet formulation were used. The effective NIR penetration depth profiles showed a wavelength dependence and strongly correlated with the reflection spectra of the top layers. In conclusion, the temperature dependence of the spectral data and the effective NIR penetration depth are useful for the design of NIR calibration models.

articles.title: Comprehensive Analysis of Allometric Scaling Exponents for Human CL and Vdss Using PXB Mice and a Proposed Method for Vdss Prediction.
articles.abstract: Reliable pharmacokinetic (PK) translation into humans is a cornerstone of first-in-human (FIH) dose selection, providing the exposure estimates needed to design efficient and informative early clinical trials. To predict human PK parameters conventional approaches include in vitro-in vivo extrapolation (IVIVE) and animal allometric scaling. The emergence of humanized liver PXB mice provides a new translational platform for predicting human clearance (CL) and steady-state volume of distribution (Vdss), typically by applying allometric scaling with fixed exponents of 0.75 for CL and 1.0 for Vdss. Previous evaluations generally applied fixed exponents without rigorous, data-driven validation of their robustness. In this study, we performed a systematic, data-science-driven assessment of the allometric exponents for human CL and Vdss derived from PXB mice data by iteratively varying dataset combinations and optimizing exponent values. Our results showed that the CL allometric relationship was highly robust across dataset combination and that the conventional 0.75 exponent is reliable. In contrast, Vdss predictions were markedly dataset dependent and the conventional 1.0 exponent was not stable. Based on these results, we investigated a new method for predicting Vdss. The compounds were grouped according to readily available data of PXB mice, and then subgroup specific allometric exponents were determined. One of these predictive models - grouping by fingerprints - substantially improved accuracy compared with the conventional approach; this was proven by repeated cross-validation. Hence, combining conventional CL and proposed Vdss prediction approach enhances confidence in FIH dosing decisions and offers a practical framework to improve translational pharmacokinetic prediction in drug discovery. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: Using a systematic, data-science driven assessment, this study confirmed the 0.75 exponent in the allometric equation for CL via PXB mice is robust, whereas the 1.0 Vdss exponent is shown to be unstable. By determining subgroup-specific allometric exponents through fingerprint grouping, the proposed method significantly improved prediction accuracy-as validated by repeated cross-validation-offering a more precise, quantitative framework for informing human FIH dose selection compared to conventional fixed-exponent approaches.

articles.title: Interindividual variability in hepatic hydrolytic enzymes: Effects of age, sex, and race on the abundance of drug-metabolizing hydrolases.
articles.abstract: Hydrolases represent a diverse class of drug-metabolizing enzymes that catalyze the hydrolytic cleavage of a broad spectrum of xenobiotics including certain novel drug modalities, thereby modulating pharmacokinetics and potentially influencing pharmacodynamics. However, many hydrolases remain poorly characterized, and their developmental expression and interindividual variability are not well understood. This study aimed to systematically characterize hydrolase expression in the human liver. Human hepatocytes obtained from 8 adult and 50 pediatric donors were subjected to global proteomics analysis to quantify hydrolase abundance and assess variability across demographic factors. Two hundred and thirty-nine hydrolases were studied for the influence of age, sex, and race on their abundance. The key enzymes included arylacetamide deacetylase (AADAC), alpha/beta hydrolase domain-containing protein 10 (ABHD10), alkaline phosphatase, tissue-nonspecific isozyme (ALPL), acyl-peptide hydrolase (APEH), bleomycin hydrolase (BLMH), valacyclovir hydrolase (BPHL), cytidine deaminase (CDA), carboxylesterase 1 (CES1), CES2, carboxymethylenebutenolidase homolog (CMBL), cathepsin A (CTSA), cathepsin B (CTSB), dipeptidyl peptidase 4 (DPP4), epoxide hydrolase 1 (EPHX1), EPHX2, EPHX3, guanine deaminase (GDA), paraoxonase 1 (PON1), PON2, PON3, and deoxynucleoside triphosphate triphosphohydrolase SAMHD1 (SAMHD1). Notably, several enzymes exhibited age-dependent increases in the abundance from neonates to adults (fold), including CDA (>200), GDA (53), CES1 (14), EPHX3 (12), ALPL (10), CES2 (3.5), sialate O-acetylesterase (SIAE) (3), and CMBL (2.6). In contrast, BLMH, CTSA, DPP4, PON2, and SAMHD1 displayed approximately 2-fold to 3-fold lower abundance in adults than in neonates. PON1 was 42% higher in Black individuals compared with White individuals, whereas PON3 abundance was 32% higher in males than in females. This study provides the first systematic quantitative characterization of a broad panel of hydrolases and provides a key foundation for physiologically-based pharmacokinetic and quantitative systems pharmacology modeling of the substrates of hydrolytic enzymes. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: Interindividual variability, including ontogeny, is well characterized for many drug-metabolizing enzymes but remains poorly defined for most hydrolases. The influence of age, sex, and race on 239 hepatic hydrolases was evaluated, revealing important demographic determinants. These data provide a critical foundation for physiologically-based pharmacokinetic modeling. Incorporation of proteomics-informed variability into physiologically-based pharmacokinetic models has the potential to improve the prediction of drug pharmacokinetics, particularly in pediatric populations.

articles.title: Safety evaluation of diester diterpenoid alkaloids and calcium oxalate needle crystals in Huafeng Dan Yaomu and the detoxification mechanism of fermentation.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Huafeng Dan is a traditional Chinese medicinal formula with over 370 years of clinical use and is listed as a National Intangible Cultural Heritage. Its core component, "Yaomu" (medicinal precursor), is prepared through a distinctive fermentation process from four toxic raw herbs recorded in the Chinese Pharmacopoeia, namely Aconitum carmichaelii, Pinellia ternata, Arisaema erubescens, and Typhonium giganteum. The safety of this unconventional manufacturing paradigm featuring fermentation of raw herbs remains scientifically uncharacterized, posing a critical barrier to its modernization. AIM OF THE STUDY: To systematically evaluate the safety-relevant properties of Huafeng Dan Yaomu through integrated exposure assessment, quantitative tracking of toxicity components during fermentation, and in-vivo toxicological verification, and to explore putative detoxification mechanism of the fermentation process. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Daily human exposure to each toxic raw herb via Yaomu was calculated based on the national drug standard and compared with Pharmacopoeia recommended doses for processed products. This comparison serves only as a reference metric; therapeutic doses for processed herbs are not toxicological safety thresholds, and raw-herb exposure cannot be directly equated to the safety of orally administered processed herbal products. HPLC methods were employed to quantify diester diterpenoid alkaloids (DDAs) and their hydrolysis products in raw Aconiti Radix and Yaomu at different fermentation stages. A validated HPLC method was established to determine acid-releasable oxalate in raw herbs, processed products, and Yaomu. Acute toxicity (200-fold the clinical human dose) and 8-week subchronic toxicity (1.6-, 3.2-, and 4.9-fold rat clinical equivalent dose based on body-surface-area scaling) studies were conducted in mice and rats, respectively. RESULTS: Daily exposure to each of the four toxic raw herbs via Huafeng Dan was only 0.039 to 0.073 g, accounting for 0.43 % to 4.87 % of the Pharmacopoeia recommended daily doses for processed products. Fermentation resulted in near-complete hydrolysis of hypaconitine and aconitine in all 22 Yaomu batches, with only trace mesaconitine detected in partial batches; mesaconitine was detectable but not quantifiable (LOQ = 0.0010 %) in most positive samples and only one one-month-fermentation sample exceeded LOQ. The total DDAs were far below the limit for processed Aconiti Radix (0.040 %). HPLC chromatographic peaks with matching retention times to benzoyl-monoester alkaloid reference standards were observed; identification was based solely on retention-time matching without definitive structural confirmation. Acid-releasable oxalate contents in Yaomu (0.60 %-1.01 %) were comparable to those in processed A. erubescens and T. giganteum, with no significant reduction during fermentation. No mortality or treatment-related adverse findings were observed in the acute limit-test at 200-fold clinical dose, nor in the 8-week subchronic study up to 4.9-fold rat clinical equivalent dose using finished Huafeng Dan. CONCLUSIONS: Inferred safety-relevant properties of Yaomu are underpinned by a dual mechanism. Extremely low daily exposure constitutes the primary safety barrier, while fermentation-mediated near-complete hydrolysis of DDAs is hypothesised to generate low-toxicity benzoyl-monoester alkaloids and provides a secondary qualitative safety enhancement, though direct confirmatory experimental evidence remains absent. Despite stable acid-releasable oxalate levels, their minimal daily intake suggests minimal irritancy risk. This integrated evaluation framework offers a transferable paradigm for safety assessment of fermented traditional medicines containing toxic ingredients.

articles.title: Potential targets and mechanisms of Di(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate exposure in inducing chronic kidney disease: a multimodal study integrating epidemiology, network toxicology, and Mendelian randomization.
articles.abstract: Di(2-ethylhexyl) phthalate (DEHP) is a widely used plasticizer present in numerous consumer and medical products and has been associated with adverse effects in multiple organ systems, including the kidney. Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is an increasing global health burden, yet the molecular targets potentially linking DEHP exposure to CKD remain incompletely understood. This study integrated epidemiological analysis, network toxicology, Mendelian randomization (MR), molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations to investigate potential molecular targets associated with DEHP exposure and CKD. Data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) were used to examine the association between urinary DEHP metabolites and CKD. DEHP-related and CKD-related targets were subsequently integrated to identify shared targets, followed by PPI network analysis and expression-based evaluation to prioritize candidate genes. MR analysis was then performed to assess the association between genetically proxied candidate genes and CKD. Molecular docking was used to explore the potential interactions between DEHP and the prioritized proteins, and molecular dynamics simulations were performed to further evaluate the structural stability of the predicted DEHP-CTSK complex. Higher urinary DEHP metabolite levels were associated with a higher prevalence of CKD. Four candidate genes-CTSK, ABL1, BCL2L1, and CCND1-were prioritized based on network and expression-based analyses. Among these genes, genetically proxied CTSK showed a significant positive association with CKD in the primary MR analysis. Molecular docking showed favorable predicted docking scores for DEHP with the four candidate proteins, while molecular dynamics simulations supported the structural stability of the predicted DEHP-CTSK complex over 100 ns. These findings provide convergent epidemiological, genetic, and computational evidence supporting CTSK as a candidate molecular target for further investigation in the context of DEHP-associated renal injury.

articles.title: Hydroxysafflor yellow A attenuates microcirculatory disturbance in MAFLD via the EGFR/MAPK1 pathway.
articles.abstract: The incidence of metabolic-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) continues to rise, making it a leading cause of chronic liver disease worldwide. Its pathological progression is frequently accompanied by microcirculatory dysfunction. However, effective therapeutic interventions targeting this specific process remain limited. Hydroxysafflor yellow A (HSYA) is the primary active component of Carthamus tinctorius L. It exerts diverse pharmacological effects, including anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and microcirculation-improving activities. However, the specific mechanisms by which HSYA regulates microcirculatory dysfunction in MAFLD have yet to be elucidated. In this study, a rat model of MAFLD was established using a methionine choline-deficient (MCD) diet to investigate the protective effects of HSYA and the underlying EGFR/MAPK1 signaling mechanism. The results showed that HSYA treatment significantly reduced serum levels of ALT, AST, TC, TG, and ET-1, while increasing NO levels. HSYA administration also expanded mesenteric microvascular diameter and accelerated blood flow velocity. Furthermore, HSYA alleviated hepatic steatosis and inflammatory injury. These effects were accompanied by the downregulation of EGFR, MAPK1, and VEGF expressions in the liver, thereby inhibiting the overactivation of the EGFR/MAPK1 pathway. In summary, HSYA effectively ameliorates hepatic injury and microcirculatory dysfunction in MAFLD rats. The underlying mechanism is associated with inhibiting the overactivation of the EGFR/MAPK1 signaling pathway and downregulating VEGF expression, which collectively restores the balance of microvascular structure and function. These findings provide experimental evidence for the therapeutic potential of HSYA in treating MAFLD-related microcirculatory disorders.

articles.title: Appetitive Pavlovian conditioned approach to reward location is reduced by both adrenergic and NMDA receptor antagonism at memory reconsolidation.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE: Appetitive Pavlovian cues can drive maladaptive reward seeking via stimulus-reward memories. Disrupting memory reconsolidation offers a potential strategy to reduce their influence, but evidence for β-adrenergic blockade with propranolol is inconsistent across behavioural paradigms, particularly relative to NMDA receptor antagonism. OBJECTIVES: We tested whether propranolol disrupts reconsolidation of appetitive sucrose memories in a paradigm involving discriminative pavlovian conditioned approach to the reward location, and compared its effects with those of the most commonly used NMDA receptor antagonist, MK-801. METHODS: Adult Lister hooded rats underwent discriminative Pavlovian conditioning. Thirty minutes before a brief memory reminder (non-reinforced or reinforced), rats received systemic drug treatment or saline control. In study 1, MK-801 (0.1 mg/kg) was administered to male rats. In study 2, propranolol (10 mg/kg) was administered to equal numbers of male and female rats. Discriminative approach to the reward location was tested drug-free at 1 and 8 days. RESULTS: In study 1, MK-801 impaired subsequent discriminated responding at test. These effects were observed not only when reminder was non-reinforced as in previous successful demonstrations, but also with reinforced reminder. In study 2, Propranolol also impaired subsequent conditioned approach, regardless of reminder type, and the effects were consistent across sexes. CONCLUSIONS: Propranolol and MK-801 can both disrupt reconsolidation of appetitive pavlovian memories under conditions that promote memory destabilisation. These findings demonstrate that β-adrenergic blockade can impair appetitive memory reconsolidation in a paradigm of conditioned approach to the reward location, challenging prior null findings and revitalising the potential for propranolol-based interventions in maladaptive reward-seeking behaviours.

articles.title: Investigating Potential Adverse Drug Reactions of Lisdexamfetamine Using Sequence Symmetry Analysis.
articles.abstract: The prevalence of ADHD is increasing rapidly, and lisdexamfetamine is increasingly popular, but few studies investigate its safety. We performed a sequence symmetry analysis (SSA) using Danish register data to identify potential ADRs associated with lisdexamfetamine in 2013-2023. Outcomes were incident prescriptions or incident discharge diagnoses. We calculated trend-adjusted sequence ratios (SR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI). We additionally performed two comparator SSAs for the same outcomes following incident use of stimulants (methylphenidate and dexamfetamine) or non-stimulants (guanfacine and atomoxetine). This study is reported according to RECORD-PE guidelines. We included 48 740 incident lisdexamfetamine users with a median age of 24 years (IQR 16-35). SRs were calculated for 1426 exposure-diagnosis and 1337 exposure-prescription pairs. The 50 highest SRs from each category were evaluated. Among these, 28 exposure-outcome combinations had a 95% CI lower bound above 1. Of the 100 outcomes, 33 were considered known ADRs, while 60 were previously unknown. Two outcomes indicating increased urinary symptoms were identified ('hematuria', SR: 1.88 [95% CI: 1.25; 2.85] and 'other urinary symptoms', SR: 1.63 [1.20; 2.23]). We also identified serious gastrointestinal outcomes as a potential safety alert. Further investigation into these symptoms as potential ADRs is warranted.

articles.title: Cenobamate in Dravet syndrome with electrophysiologically confirmed SCN1A loss-of-function variants: long-term real-world follow-up.
articles.abstract: Dravet syndrome (DS) is a severe developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (DEE) characterized by seizures and developmental delay/regression, primarily caused by loss-of-function (LoF) variants in the SCN1A gene, which encodes the Nav1.1 sodium channel. Hyperexcitability in DS results from impaired inhibitory interneuron function. Sodium channel blockers are considered to be contraindicated particularly in the long-term treatment of patients with LoF variants in sodium channels as they may exacerbate seizures. However, we previously reported that cenobamate (CNB), an anti-seizure medication thought to be contraindicated due to its sodium channel blocking action, was effective in treating adult DS patients. These patients displayed a typical DS phenotype. Extended long-term follow-up demonstrated sustained clinical benefit of CNB treatment. To functionally characterize the previously unclassified patient-specific SCN1A variants, we conducted electrophysiological and localization studies using HEK cells expressing Nav1.1. Whole-cell patch-clamp recordings confirmed that the patient variants were LoF, ranging from markedly reduced to nearly absent peak sodium currents. Acute CNB exposure did not alter peak sodium current density under the experimental conditions used. These findings demonstrate sustained clinical benefit of CNB in adults with genetically confirmed DS carrying electrophysiologically confirmed LoF SCN1A variants and further expand the clinical experience with CNB in this patient population.

articles.title: Carnosic acid alleviates high-altitude cerebral edema by suppressing oxidative stress and microglia activation-induced neuroinflammation.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Oxidative stress and neuroinflammation constitute key pathological contributors to high-altitude cerebral edema (HACE). Carnosic acid (CA) exerts important roles in neurodegeneration and brain injury, but its function in HACE remains elusive. METHODS: High-altitude hypobaric hypoxic (HH)-mimicked HACE rats were administered carnosic acid. The effects on hematological parameter changes, blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability, energetic metabolism disorder, cognitive and motor impairment, oxidative stress, and microglia-mediated neuroinflammation were explored. The function of carnosic acid in microglia-mediated damage to astrocytes and endothelial cells under hypoxia was investigated. RESULTS: Carnosic acid dose-dependently normalized aberrant hematological parameter changes, brain water content, and histopathological changes in HH-mimicked HACE rats. Moreover, HH conditions enhanced BBB permeability and BBB-related aquaporin 4 (AQP4) expression and decreased BBB-related occludin and zonula occludens-1 (ZO-1) expression, which were reversed after carnosic acid. Carnosic acid alleviated energetic metabolism disorder and improved cognitive and motor impairment in HACE rats. Carnosic acid attenuated HH-evoked oxidative stress by inhibiting reactive oxygen species (ROS) and malondialdehyde levels and increased antioxidant glutathione and superoxide dismutase levels. Carnosic acid suppressed HH-induced microglia activation and pro-inflammatory response. Additionally, aberrant activation of the NF-κB-NLRP3 inflammasome axis in HACE rats was also inhibited by carnosic acid. Carnosic acid inhibited hypoxia-induced pro-inflammatory microglia activation by the NF-κB-NLRP3 pathway. Moreover, carnosic acid also attenuated hypoxia-activated microglia-induced AQP4 expression in astrocytes and damage to the endothelial tight junction. CONCLUSION: Carnosic acid may attenuate the pathological progression of HACE by restraining oxidative stress and microglia activation-induced neuroinflammation via the NF-κB-NLRP3 axis, supporting it as a promising neuroprotective intervention for HACE.

articles.title: The ratio of propylene glycol to glycerol modulates nicotine taste and reward: more glycerol, more reward.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Propylene glycol (PG) and glycerol (Gly) are odorless tobacco product constituents that act as solvents in electronic cigarette e-liquids and as humectants in oral nicotine products. Little is known about how PG/Gly ratio may affect nicotine's sensory and rewarding properties. To address this gap, we utilized the taste reactivity test and four-bottle choice test to investigate the impact of PG/Gly ratio on nicotine's taste and reward. METHODS: A taste reactivity test was performed using young adult rats that received oral infusions of water, nicotine (10 μg/mL) and various PG/Gly ratios in the absence and presence of nicotine via intraoral catheters. Facial responses to each infusion were video recorded and the ingestive and aversive taste responses to each solution were scored and analyzed. In a separate cohort of rats, a four-bottle choice test was utilized to assess preference for various PG/Gly ratios with or without nicotine. RESULTS: Young adult rats exhibited higher aversive reactions to PG100/Gly0 alone. Higher Gly content (PG0/Gly100 with nicotine) increased ingestive responses compared to nicotine alone. Higher Gly content (PG20/Gly80 with nicotine and PG0/Gly100 with nicotine) decreased aversive reactions compared to nicotine alone. Young adult rats also displayed greater preference for PG0/Gly100 alone and PG0/Gly100 with nicotine compared to vehicle water and nicotine, respectively. CONCLUSION: Overall, nicotine's ingestive and aversive taste was altered by PG and Gly depending on the ratio. Specifically, higher Gly enhanced nicotine's hedonic value and reduced nicotine's aversive properties in both sexes. Higher Gly content was also preferred during the four-bottle choice test alone and in the presence of nicotine. Together, our results suggests that PG/Gly ratio, particularly high Gly content, influences nicotine's abuse liability.

articles.title: Early adjunctive vasopressin was not associated with a lower 7-day risk of renal replacement therapy in norepinephrine-treated patients with cirrhosis: a target-trial-informed study with external replication.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Early adjunctive vasopressin can reduce catecholamine exposure in vasodilatory shock, but whether it prevents severe kidney failure in norepinephrine-treated patients with cirrhosis is uncertain. METHODS: We conducted a target-trial-informed landmark study using MIMIC-IV as the primary cohort and eICU-CRD as an external replication cohort. Adults with a first intensive care unit admission, cirrhosis or advanced chronic liver disease, and norepinephrine initiation within 24 h of admission were eligible. Treatment was classified at a 6-h landmark as vasopressin initiated within 6 h of norepinephrine or no vasopressin during that window; patients in the latter group could receive vasopressin later. The primary outcome was new renal replacement therapy (RRT) between the landmark and day 7. Propensity-score overlap weighting was prespecified as the primary analysis. RESULTS: The MIMIC-IV cohort included 1,086 patients (early vasopressin, n = 295; no early vasopressin, n = 791), and the eICU-CRD cohort included 356 patients (n = 91 and n = 265, respectively). Before weighting, vasopressin recipients had greater shock and liver-disease severity. Early vasopressin was not associated with lower odds of new RRT in MIMIC-IV (overlap-weighted odds ratio [OR] 1.37, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.83-2.26; P = 0.214), eICU-CRD (OR 1.10, 95% CI 0.45-2.69; P = 0.833), or the pooled analysis (OR 1.30, 95% CI 0.84-2.01; P = 0.235). Mortality was higher among early-vasopressin recipients, but this secondary association remained highly vulnerable to confounding by indication. Weighted absolute-risk estimates, cumulative RRT incidence, subgroup analyses, and sensitivity analyses provided no supporting renal-benefit signal; creatinine trajectories were evaluated descriptively because follow-up measurements were susceptible to survivor selection. CONCLUSION: Among norepinephrine-treated patients with cirrhosis or advanced chronic liver disease who were alive and RRT-free 6 h after norepinephrine initiation, early adjunctive vasopressin was not associated with less RRT by day 7. The findings do not challenge vasopressin use for hemodynamic support when clinically indicated, but do not support early initiation solely as a renal-protective strategy.

articles.title: Functional-genomic prioritization identifies MED12 as a candidate RNAi vulnerability in acute myeloid leukemia: evaluation of a T22 peptide-functionalized LNP-siRNA formulation.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) depends in part on transcriptional and epigenetic programs that can be difficult to target with conventional small molecules. RNA interference provides a potential approach to perturb such vulnerabilities, but target selection and intracellular siRNA delivery remain major challenges. METHODS: Public dependency datasets and primary AML and normal hematopoietic expression resources were integrated to prioritize candidate RNAi vulnerabilities. A T22 peptide-functionalized lipid nanoparticle (TLNP) formulation carrying siMED12 was evaluated in OCI-AML3 cells, with RT-qPCR and CCK-8 validation in THP-1 cells. A systemic OCI-AML3 mouse model was used for exploratory assessment of survival and tolerability. RESULTS: MED12 ranked highest in the integrated functional-genomic prioritization framework. In OCI-AML3 and THP-1 cells, TLNP-siMED12 produced replicated reductions in MED12 transcript abundance and cell viability across three independently initiated experiments. In OCI-AML3 cells, cellular uptake, free T22 competition, immunoblotting, apoptosis, migration and whole-well crystal violet-stained colony-like focus observations were each obtained once and are reported descriptively. In the systemic model, TLNP-siMED12 treatment was associated with prolonged survival; body weight, endpoint blood measurements and illustrative H&E images provided limited tolerability information. CONCLUSION: Integrated functional-genomic prioritization identified MED12 as a candidate RNAi vulnerability in AML. TLNP-siMED12 produced reproducible transcript and viability responses in the evaluated AML models and was associated with prolonged survival in the systemic OCI-AML3 model. Hematopoietic selectivity, receptor-dependent delivery and in vivo target engagement remain to be established.

articles.title: Formononetin improved healthspan via the P53/P21/CDK4 pathway in SAMP8 mice and DAF-16/SKN-1 signaling pathway in C.elegans.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To investigate the healthy aging effects of Formononetin and its underlying molecular mechanisms. METHODS: SAMP8 mice were administered Formononetin (4, 8, 16 mg/kg, po) for 5 months. Behavioral tests were performed in 9-month-old mice, followed by histopathology. 5-methylcytosine (5-mC) level in the brain were detected by immunofluorescence, aging-related protein expression was measured by Western blot. In C. elegans, the lifespan, stress resistance, and aging-related gene expressions were assessed. Mutant strains (daf-16 and skn-1) were used to verify pathway dependency. RESULTS: Formononetin dose-dependently ameliorated cognitive deficits, anxiety-like behaviors, and motor decline in SAMP8 mice, attenuated neuronal damage in the hippocampal CA1, DG and cerebral cortex, reversed 5-mC level, downregulated protein expression of P53, P21, while upregulated CDK4 and Nrf2. In C. elegans, Formononetin (37.30 μmol/L) significantly extended lifespan under normal, thermal stress, and oxidative stress conditions, improved locomotion, reduced lipofuscin accumulation, increased total SOD activity, and upregulated skn-1, sir-2.1, daf-16 and sod-3 mRNA. No lifespan extension was observed in daf-16 or skn-1 mutants. CONCLUSION: Formononetin effectively attenuated cognitive deficits, ameliorated neuronal damage and increased 5-mC level, possibly via regulated P53, P21, CDK4 and Nrf2 protein expression in the brain of SAMP8 mice. In C. elegans, Formononetin extended lifespan, increased stress resistance, and improved locomotion and lipofuscin accumulation, possibly via regulated expression of DAF-16 and SKN-1.

articles.title: Depleted before the dose: the mitochondrial vulnerability threshold hypothesis for fluoroquinolone-associated multisystem toxicity.
articles.abstract: Fluoroquinolone (FQ) antibiotics have an established capacity for mitochondrial injury, yet only a subset of exposed patients develop severe or persistent toxicity. We propose the Mitochondrial Vulnerability Threshold (MVT) hypothesis: that whether a standard therapeutic FQ dose produces clinically significant toxicity may depend substantially on the patient's pre-existing mitochondrial reserve capacity rather than on fixed pharmacological properties alone. Although this toxicity was first recognized through musculoskeletal injury-particularly tendinopathy and tendon rupture-the reported syndrome extends to peripheral nerve, autonomic, central nervous system, and other tissues; we therefore use the term fluoroquinolone-associated multisystem toxicity (FQMT), with musculoskeletal (tendon) injury as its prototypical and best-characterized manifestation. We hypothesize that converging iatrogenic, nutritional, infectious, lifestyle, and environmental stressors-statin-associated CoQ10 depletion, proton-pump-inhibitor magnesium and B12 malabsorption, metformin-associated B12 depletion with genetically stratifiable risk, physical inactivity, metabolic syndrome, post-COVID-19 mitochondrial injury, antibiotic-induced dysbiosis, and environmental toxin burden-may contribute to higher apparent vulnerability in contemporary prescribing populations. We do not claim to demonstrate a temporal increase in FQMT incidence or severity; this is presented as a testable proposition. We further outline, as a speculative and explicitly unvalidated mechanism, whether epigenetic modification of the mitochondrial DNA displacement loop (D-loop) could contribute to escalating toxicity on repeat exposure. We propose the Mitochondrial Vulnerability Score (MVS) as a candidate research instrument (not a clinical prescribing tool) and present five falsifiable predictions with study designs. We discuss, with explicit caution, whether severe FQMT might in future be considered an acquired mitochondrial disorder, and we specify the evidence that such a classification would require. All clinical, therapeutic, and prophylactic content is hypothesis-generating and requires prospective validation.

articles.title: Circulating serotonin is associated with calcific aortic valve stenosis: a two-phase metabolomics study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Calcific aortic valve stenosis (CAVS) is the most prevalent valvular heart disease in the elderly, yet no pharmacological therapy can halt its progression, partly due to incomplete understanding of disease-associated metabolic alterations and the lack of circulating biomarkers for disease detection. OBJECTIVE: We aimed to characterize metabolic alterations associated with CAVS and evaluate a candidate circulating marker for CAVS detection.
